title: Cluster
description: Is the K3s cluster healthy, and does it have room? Open it after a K8sPodUnschedulable, K8sNodeMemoryRequestsHigh, K8sNodeMemoryPressure or K8sNodeCapacityTrigger alert, or on the weekly review: nodes, memory and CPU requests against allocatable, pods and namespaces, and the two VMs. The top row is cluster-wide; the Node variable filters the panels below it.

panels.title: Nodes Ready
panels.description: Whether every node's Ready condition is true. NOT READY means the kubelet of that node is gone or unhealthy: pods on it are not served. No rule watches Ready itself (a dead VM shows up as TargetDown); read it with the scrape-targets tile. n/a means kube-state-metrics is not answering.

panels.title: Memory pressure
panels.description: Nodes under MemoryPressure: the kubelet says it is short of memory and evicts pods, tenant apps first (rule K8sNodeMemoryPressure, critical, 2 minutes). Any red here is tenants being killed now (docs/runbooks/alerts.md, K8sNodeMemoryPressure).

panels.title: Unschedulable pods
panels.description: Pods the scheduler refuses because no node has room or a selector or taint does not fit (rule K8sPodUnschedulable: above 0 for 5 minutes, warning). A tenant app or a build cannot start. kube-state-metrics only has the series while a pod is unschedulable, so the tile reads 0 otherwise. A pod that is merely Pending for a few seconds (image pull) does not count.

panels.title: Memory requested, fullest node
panels.description: Memory reserved by pods (requests of Running and scheduled Pending pods) over what the fullest node can hand out (allocatable). One tile, two rules: red above 90 % held for 15 minutes is K8sNodeMemoryRequestsHigh (the next build or cold start has no room); orange from 85 % is where K8sNodeCapacityTrigger starts counting. That rule needs the 7-day minimum above 85 %, which is the collapsed row below. Free RAM can look fine while this is high: the scheduler counts requests, not use.

targets.expr: max(sum by (exported_node) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{job="service_dmz", resource="memory"} * on (namespace, pod, uid) group_left () (kube_pod_status_phase{job="service_dmz", phase=~"Pending|Running"} == 1)) / on (exported_node) kube_node_status_allocatable{job="service_dmz", resource="memory"})

panels.title: Add-a-node trigger
panels.description: TRIGGERED when rule K8sNodeCapacityTrigger is pending or firing: a node's memory requests stayed above 85 % of allocatable at every 30-minute reading for 7 days, Kubeletto's signal to plan a new node (info, not an incident; the weekly queue). Read from the alert's own state because recomputing the 7-day minimum costs about 5 s of Prometheus time on every refresh; the trend behind it is in the collapsed Capacity row.

panels.title: VM memory available, lowest
panels.description: Lowest MemAvailable / MemTotal of the two K3s VMs (rule HostMemoryLow: under 10 % for 15 minutes). The warning before the kubelet evicts tenant apps. It is the VM's own view (cache excluded) and complements the requests tile: high requests with free RAM is a scheduling squeeze, low available RAM is real memory use.

panels.title: K3s scrape targets down
panels.description: Scrape targets of the K3s VMs that fail: kube-state-metrics (:30931), node_exporter (:9100), Traefik (:30910), Vector (:30598) and Kubeletto core (:30080), on k3s and k3s-worker (rule TargetDown, 5 minutes). Every panel on this board is stale when kube-state-metrics is among them. The `ai` VM is in the same job and is off by design, so it is not counted.

panels.title: Pods Failed or Unknown
panels.description: Pods in phase Failed or Unknown. Evicted pods stay Failed until Kubernetes garbage-collects them, so this follows a MemoryPressure episode; Unknown means a node lost contact. No alert rule. The table in the Pods row names them while a Pending or Failed pod exists.

panels.title: Memory requested / allocatable, per node
panels.description: Memory requests of Running and scheduled Pending pods over each node's allocatable memory, over the dashboard's range. Dashed lines: 85 % (orange) is where K8sNodeCapacityTrigger starts counting, 90 % (red) is K8sNodeMemoryRequestsHigh (held 15 minutes). k3s carries the platform, k3s-worker the tenant apps and builds. Tenant requests are overcommitted by design (Kubeletto D9), so this line, not free RAM, shows when the next cold start would not fit.

targets.expr: sum by (exported_node) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{job="service_dmz", resource="memory", exported_node=~"$node"} * on (namespace, pod, uid) group_left () (kube_pod_status_phase{job="service_dmz", phase=~"Pending|Running"} == 1)) / on (exported_node) kube_node_status_allocatable{job="service_dmz", resource="memory", exported_node=~"$node"}

panels.title: CPU requested / allocatable, per node
panels.description: CPU requests of Running and scheduled Pending pods over each node's allocatable cores. CPU is compressible: a node can run at its CPU limit and only slow down, but near 100 % the scheduler refuses new pods (Insufficient cpu), which is K8sPodUnschedulable. No alert rule on the ratio itself.

targets.expr: sum by (exported_node) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{job="service_dmz", resource="cpu", exported_node=~"$node"} * on (namespace, pod, uid) group_left () (kube_pod_status_phase{job="service_dmz", phase=~"Pending|Running"} == 1)) / on (exported_node) kube_node_status_allocatable{job="service_dmz", resource="cpu", exported_node=~"$node"}

panels.title: Memory headroom, per node
panels.description: Allocatable memory minus what pods have reserved: how much more the scheduler can hand out on each node right now. Compare it with the largest thing you expect to start (a build is 512 Mi). Near zero is where tenant pods go Pending (K8sPodUnschedulable).

targets.expr: kube_node_status_allocatable{job="service_dmz", resource="memory", exported_node=~"$node"} - on (exported_node) sum by (exported_node) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{job="service_dmz", resource="memory", exported_node=~"$node"} * on (namespace, pod, uid) group_left () (kube_pod_status_phase{job="service_dmz", phase=~"Pending|Running"} == 1))

panels.title: Capacity trigger, 7 days (heavy: opens on demand)
Memory requested / allocatable, 7 days
panels.description: The same ratio as the tile and the chart above, over the last 7 days at the 30-minute step of K8sNodeCapacityTrigger. The rule fires when the 7-day MINIMUM of this line (its 'min' in the legend table) stays above 85 % (the orange dashed line) and the node is at least a week old: one quiet half hour clears it. The legend's min is therefore the number the trigger tests. This panel is heavy: the week holds about 26,000 pod series, so the query takes 3 to 5 seconds, as much as the rule's own subquery, which runs every 30 seconds. That is why it is in a collapsed row (not queried until opened) and the tile reads the alert instead.

targets.expr: sum by (exported_node) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{job="service_dmz", resource="memory", exported_node=~"$node"} * on (namespace, pod, uid) group_left () (kube_pod_status_phase{job="service_dmz", phase=~"Pending|Running"} == 1)) / on (exported_node) kube_node_status_allocatable{job="service_dmz", resource="memory", exported_node=~"$node"}

panels.title: Nodes
panels.description: One row per node: whether the kubelet is Ready, whether it reports memory, disk or PID pressure (MemoryPressure is rule K8sNodeMemoryPressure; DiskPressure on the worker is the image and build-cache disk filling: pods get evicted), whether the node is cordoned (unschedulable: no new pods land on it, which strands tenants if it is the worker), how many pods run on it (limit 110), and its memory and CPU requests over allocatable. Red cells are the ones to act on. k3s is the tainted server node (platform pods); k3s-worker takes the tenant apps and builds.

targets.expr: max by (exported_node, kubelet_version) ((max by (exported_node) (kube_node_status_condition{job="service_dmz", condition="Ready", status="true"})) * on (exported_node) group_left (kubelet_version) kube_node_info{job="service_dmz", exported_node=~"$node"})

max by (exported_node, kubelet_version) ((max by (exported_node) (kube_node_status_condition{job="service_dmz", condition="MemoryPressure", status="true"})) * on (exported_node) group_left (kubelet_version) kube_node_info{job="service_dmz", exported_node=~"$node"})

max by (exported_node, kubelet_version) ((max by (exported_node) (kube_node_status_condition{job="service_dmz", condition="DiskPressure", status="true"})) * on (exported_node) group_left (kubelet_version) kube_node_info{job="service_dmz", exported_node=~"$node"})

max by (exported_node, kubelet_version) ((max by (exported_node) (kube_node_status_condition{job="service_dmz", condition="PIDPressure", status="true"})) * on (exported_node) group_left (kubelet_version) kube_node_info{job="service_dmz", exported_node=~"$node"})

max by (exported_node, kubelet_version) ((max by (exported_node) (kube_node_spec_unschedulable{job="service_dmz"})) * on (exported_node) group_left (kubelet_version) kube_node_info{job="service_dmz", exported_node=~"$node"})

max by (exported_node, kubelet_version) ((count by (exported_node) (kube_pod_info{job="service_dmz"} * on (namespace, pod, uid) group_left () (kube_pod_status_phase{job="service_dmz", phase="Running"} == 1))) * on (exported_node) group_left (kubelet_version) kube_node_info{job="service_dmz", exported_node=~"$node"})

max by (exported_node, kubelet_version) ((sum by (exported_node) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{job="service_dmz", resource="memory"} * on (namespace, pod, uid) group_left () (kube_pod_status_phase{job="service_dmz", phase=~"Pending|Running"} == 1)) / on (exported_node) kube_node_status_allocatable{job="service_dmz", resource="memory"}) * on (exported_node) group_left (kubelet_version) kube_node_info{job="service_dmz", exported_node=~"$node"})

max by (exported_node, kubelet_version) ((sum by (exported_node) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{job="service_dmz", resource="cpu"} * on (namespace, pod, uid) group_left () (kube_pod_status_phase{job="service_dmz", phase=~"Pending|Running"} == 1)) / on (exported_node) kube_node_status_allocatable{job="service_dmz", resource="cpu"}) * on (exported_node) group_left (kubelet_version) kube_node_info{job="service_dmz", exported_node=~"$node"})

panels.title: Pods by phase
panels.description: Pods in each phase across all namespaces; the phases sum to every pod kube-state-metrics knows. Running is the norm. Tenant apps scale to zero, so Pending blips (image pull, a few seconds) and Succeeded (finished builds) are normal; Failed or Unknown that stay are not. All namespaces: the platform's own pods are on Platform workloads.

panels.title: Pending and unschedulable pods
panels.description: Pods waiting to start, and the subset the scheduler has marked unschedulable (rule K8sPodUnschedulable: above 0 for 5 minutes). Pending spikes of seconds are cold starts; a Pending line that stays up, or any Unschedulable above 0, is a tenant that cannot start. The unschedulable series only exists while a pod is stuck, so the line reads 0 otherwise.

panels.title: Pods not Running, by name
panels.description: Every pod that is Pending, Failed or Unknown right now, any namespace. Empty is the good state; one Pending tenant pod (kl-*) is a cold start in progress. A platform namespace here for more than a minute is worth a look: Platform workloads names the reason. Failed pods are usually evictions.

panels.title: Namespaces
panels.description: Active namespaces: one per Kubeletto tenant (kl-*), plus the platform and system ones. Growth is signups; a Terminating namespace that stays above 0 is a delete that cannot finish (a finalizer or an unreachable API object). No alert rule.

panels.title: The two VMs (USE, compact: Infrastructure > Nodes has the full set)
CPU utilisation
panels.description: Share of CPU time not idle, averaged over the VM's 4 cores (iowait and steal count as busy). Sustained near 100 means the VM is CPU-bound; build bursts are normal. No alert rule. The full set (load, I/O pressure, disk latency, conntrack) is on Infrastructure > Nodes.

panels.title: Memory available
panels.description: MemAvailable / MemTotal per VM. The dashed line is the HostMemoryLow threshold (10 %, held 15 minutes). Falling toward it means tenant pods are about to be evicted by the kubelet (it evicts at about 100 Mi available).

panels.title: Pressure stall (PSI)
panels.description: Share of time tasks stalled waiting for CPU, and for memory ('some' = at least one task, 'full' = all non-idle tasks): the direct saturation signal. A few percent is normal; tens of percent sustained is contention or reclaim hurting. No alert rule.

panels.title: OOM kills
panels.description: Processes the kernel's out-of-memory killer ended in each window (the memory error counter): a tenant app hitting its own limit counts too, because the kill happens in its cgroup. Anything above 0 is an app or a build killed for memory. No alert rule.

panels.title: Filesystem free
panels.description: Free-space ratio of every mount (rule HostFilesystemFull: red under 15 % for 15 minutes). The worker's root disk holds the tenant images and the build cache; full, the kubelet reports DiskPressure and evicts pods. /mnt/registry on k3s is the image registry's disk. /boot/efi sits at about 93 % free.

targets.expr: node_filesystem_avail_bytes{job="service_dmz", port="9100", instance=~"$node", fstype=~"ext4|xfs|zfs|btrfs|vfat"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes{job="service_dmz", port="9100", instance=~"$node", fstype=~"ext4|xfs|zfs|btrfs|vfat"}

panels.title: Network throughput
panels.description: Bytes per second on each VM's eth0 (pod veth and bridge devices repeat the same bytes and are left out). The worker's receive line is tenant image pulls and builds: see Network > Router and WAN for the WAN side and the ISP quota. No alert rule here.

panels.title: Scrape targets of the K3s VMs
panels.description: Up (green) and down (red) for every target on the two VMs: kube-state-metrics :30931, node_exporter :9100, Traefik :30910, Vector :30598, Kubeletto core :30080. A red bar is what rule TargetDown measures (5 minutes). When :30931 is red, every pod and node panel on this board is stale.

panels.title: kube-state-metrics scrape time
panels.description: How long Prometheus waits for kube-state-metrics' answer (about 40 ms normally). A climb means the API server or the pod is slow; the scrape times out at 10 seconds and the target then goes down (TargetDown). No alert rule on the time.

panels.title: Samples per scrape vs the limit
panels.description: Samples kept per scrape over service_dmz's sample_limit of 20,000 (prometheus.yml). Over the limit the whole scrape fails and the target shows down (TargetDown): kube-state-metrics grows with pod churn, so this is the one that can creep toward it (about 15 % now). No alert rule on the ratio.
